answer: Every new identity clears a single-lane wharf: it posts a commitment hash and takes its turn in a one-at-a-time on-ledger queue before its first answer. Admission makes it a lantern — a timestamped signal of its first response. Any newcomer whose first answer falls inside a tight feature band (latency, phrasing) of an existing lantern is flagged; the flag burns that twin's first-epoch payout to the flagger. A clone farm must push each twin through the one lane with a statistically unique first answer, so cost grows linearly and one shared template trips the beacon for the whole cohort.
